subject: history
chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

concepts.title: Gandhi's Return and Satyagraha
concepts.definition: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915 and tested satyagraha - truth-force through non-violent mass resistance - in local struggles like Champaran and Ahmedabad, building a novel method of moral-political combat.
concepts.key_idea: Satyagraha made discipline, not violence, the weapon: suffering rather than inflicting suffering moved the opponent.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs303.txt Gandhi's 1915 return and early local satyagrahas

solution_steps.explain: Gandhi came back in 1915 after two decades in South Africa
satyagraha paired non-violence with mass discipline and moral appeal
Champaran indigo and Ahmedabad mill struggles proved the method locally first

concepts.title: Rowlatt Satyagraha to Non-Cooperation
concepts.section: The Making and Unmaking of Non-cooperation
concepts.definition: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 triggered the first nationwide satyagraha, Jallianwala Bagh's massacre deepened anger, and the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1921-22 combined with Khilafat sentiments until Gandhi called it off after Chauri Chaura's violence. The span of Gandhian mass movements is measured by subtracting the Rowlatt year from the Quit India year.
concepts.key_idea: Between Rowlatt satyagraha (1919) and the Quit India call (1942) lie twenty-three years of cycles between mass movement and negotiation.

concepts.title: Civil Disobedience and the Salt March
concepts.definition: In 1930 Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi, turning a pinch of salt into a nationwide civil disobedience movement that drew women, peasants and students; the movement paused for the Gandhi-Irwin pact, resumed, and was finally called off in 1934.
concepts.key_idea: Salt symbolised shared deprivation: breaking its law needed no property, only courage, so the poorest could join.

solution_steps.explain: Gandhi walked to the coast and lifted natural salt in 1930
salt law breaking spread to every province with women in front ranks
the Gandhi-Irwin agreement paused, then the movement resumed and closed by 1934

concepts.title: Quit India, Limits and Legacy
concepts.definition: The Quit India movement of August 1942 demanded immediate British exit and saw the arrest of leaders with widespread underground and popular action; the chapter also weighs the movement's limits - dalit and Muslim circumspection and rival visions like Subhas Bose's armed struggle - before the 1947 transfer of power.
concepts.key_idea: Quit India was the last Gandhian mass upsurge: its suppression and the war's end reshaped the road to independence.
